title: Materialization boundary

title: Producer pause
prompt: P is paused for cost control, while C remains active. The consumer accesses the data through its existing internal shortcut. Permissions are unchanged. Which statement matches the documented capacity example?

options.text: The consumer can continue reading through C; producer storage remains billed to P.
options.why: Correct. The active consuming capacity supplies the transaction capacity for the shortcut read.

options.text: The shortcut automatically creates a full backup on C at pause time.
options.why: No backup operation follows from pausing a capacity.

options.text: Reads continue and storage charges stop on P.
options.why: Pausing does not remove stored bytes or their charges.

options.text: All consumer reads must fail solely because the producer storage capacity is paused.
options.why: The cross-capacity shortcut case is an explicit exception to this blanket claim.

explanation: Follow the access path and identify its consuming capacity. The video's broad capacity statement needs this cross-capacity qualification; it is not permission-free or universally available access.

title: Transaction allocation
prompt: Finance sees increased OneLake reads after C adopts an internal shortcut to P. The source bytes remain in P. Which cost allocation is consistent with the documented model?

options.text: Both storage and all shortcut reads must be allocated to P.
options.why: The internal shortcut read transaction is attributed to the consuming capacity.

options.text: Allocate source storage to P and internal-shortcut read transaction usage to C.
options.why: Correct. Storage location and consuming compute are distinct dimensions.

options.text: Allocate neither because every shortcut transaction is free.
options.why: No-copy access does not mean no transaction consumption.

options.why: A reference does not transfer ownership of the stored bytes.

title: Aggregate eligibility
prompt: An append-only SQL MLV with CDF enabled computes SUM(amount) and AVG(price) by country. Its source is unpartitioned. All other constructs are supported. Why can adding AVG change refresh behavior?

options.text: A SQL endpoint index automatically supplies the missing Spark partitioning.
options.why: SQL metadata does not satisfy the documented source partitioning condition.

options.text: SUM guarantees incremental refresh for every other expression in the same SELECT.
options.why: An eligible aggregate does not remove requirements introduced by other aggregates.

options.text: AVG is unsupported in all Spark SQL queries.
options.why: AVG is valid SQL; the issue is incremental-maintenance eligibility.

options.text: The mixed aggregate query needs the documented source partitioning and grouping conditions for incremental refresh.
options.why: Correct. AVG introduces requirements not needed for SUM alone; without them, full refresh is a supported fallback.
